title: Replit’s CEO says the future of work is the ‘self-driving company’
key_facts: Replit CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad spoke at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on Thursday.
He described a 'self-driving company' in which AI agents do much of the grunt work and people are valued for judgment and taste.
He said Replit changed how it operates after AI agents became more reliable earlier this year.
Support tickets at Replit are first examined by an agent (checking GitHub issues, the codebase and Linear tickets); a person then decides, and a fix can be deployed with a click.
He said agents are changing what people work on rather than taking jobs; staff spend more time on what to work on, whiteboarding and architecture.
He said much of America and the world does not yet know the change is coming.
quote_evidence: “Our company entirely changed how we operate, and I would say the closest analogy is a ‘self-driving company’,” Masad said.
“You have an entire loop where agents did most of the work, but crucially, there’s human judgment in the middle, and we don’t think that’s going away anytime soon.
The end result is that instead of taking jobs from people, agents are changing what people work on.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI-coding company chief describes how his own firm's work changed, but it is the company's own account.
notes: Talk given Thursday 15 Oct, before the 16 Oct window, so the score is lowered by 1 and freshness is marked. Masad's account is about his own company and he sells AI coding tools.
